from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Feedback Loop: What is Iteration?"
        lines = [
            "Iteration means feeding a function's output back as input.",
            "Imagine a number cycling through the same rule repeatedly.",
            "This feedback loop creates a sequence of evolving values."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the word 'Iteration' in #FFFFFF, then replace it with a looping arrow icon.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        iteration_text = Text("Iteration", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(iteration_text, "B3", "B4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(iteration_text))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Looping arrow icon (Arc with tip)
        loop_arrow = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=0, angle=1.5 * PI, color=WHITE).add_tip()
        self.place_in_area(loop_arrow, "B3", "B4", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(ReplacementTransform(iteration_text, loop_arrow))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show a box labeled 'Rule: $z^2 + c$' in #00FF00, with an input arrow and output arrow looping back.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        
        rule_box = Rectangle(width=2.5, height=1.2, color=GREEN)
        # Using a combination of Text and MathTex for reliability (L022)
        rule_label_text = Text("Rule: ", font_size=20, color=GREEN)
        rule_label_math = MathTex("z^2 + c", color=GREEN).scale(0.8)
        rule_label = VGroup(rule_label_text, rule_label_math).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        rule_group = VGroup(rule_box, rule_label)
        self.place_in_area(rule_group, "C3", "D4", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Input arrow
        input_arrow = Arrow(
            start=self.grid["C2"], 
            end=rule_box.get_left(), 
            color=GREEN,
            buff=0.1
        )
        # Output arrow
        output_arrow = Arrow(
            start=rule_box.get_right(), 
            end=self.grid["C5"], 
            color=GREEN,
            buff=0.1
        )
        # Feedback loop arrow (Curved arrow going under)
        feedback_arrow = CurvedArrow(
            start_point=self.grid["C5"],
            end_point=self.grid["C2"],
            angle=-PI,
            color=GREEN
        )

        self.play(
            Create(rule_box),
            Write(rule_label),
            GrowArrow(input_arrow),
            GrowArrow(output_arrow)
        )
        self.play(Create(feedback_arrow))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show a sequence of numbers (e.g., 2, 4, 16...) appearing one by one in #87CEEB.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#87CEEB")
        
        # Create sequence elements
        numbers_list = ["2", "4", "16", "256", "..."]
        num_mobjects = VGroup(*[Text(n, color="#87CEEB") for n in numbers_list]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(num_mobjects, "E2", "E5", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # Animate numbers one by one
        for num in num_mobjects:
            self.play(FadeIn(num, shift=UP * 0.2), run_time=0.5)
            self.wait(0.2)
            
        self.wait(2)

            FadeIn(dot, scale=0.5),

            run_time=1.5

class Section3Scene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        """
        Sets up the background, title, and bullet points on the left side.
        """
        # Set background
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        
        # Title at the top
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=32, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Bullet points container (Left side)
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"• {line}", font_size=24, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.7)
        
        # Grid initialization for right-side visuals
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]
        
        # Define 6x6 grid coordinates restricted to the right half of the screen
        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # x shifts to the right side (0.5 to 5.5), y spans center (-2.5 to 2.5)
                x = 1.0 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        """
        Utility to place a mobject at a specific grid coordinate.
        """
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        # Configuration for Section 3: Holomorphic Dynamics
        title_content = "Holomorphic Dynamics & Iteration"
        lecture_bullets = [
            "Complex Plane Mapping",
            "Fixed Points & Stability",
            "The Iteration z_{n+1} = f(z_n)",
            "Defining the Julia Set"
        ]

        # 1. Initialize Layout
        self.setup_layout(title_content, lecture_bullets)
        
        # Animate bullets one by one
        for bullet in self.lecture:
            self.play(FadeIn(bullet, shift=RIGHT), run_time=0.6)

        # 2. Visual Representation: Complex Mapping
        # Creating a small coordinate system on the right grid
        plane_center = self.grid["C3"]
        plane = ComplexPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=3,
            y_length=3,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        ).move_to(plane_center)

        # Function label
        func_label = MathTex("f(z) = z^2 + c", font_size=30, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(func_label, "A3")

        self.play(
            Create(plane),
            Write(func_label),
            run_time=1.5
        )

        # 3. Iteration Visualization
        # Example points: mapping z_0 -> z_1 -> z_2
        z0_val = 0.5 + 0.2j
        c_val = -0.4 + 0.3j
        
        z0_point = plane.n2p(z0_val)
        dot0 = Dot(z0_point, color=BLUE, radius=0.08)
        lbl0 = MathTex("z_0", font_size=20).next_to(dot0, UR, buff=0.05)

        self.play(FadeIn(dot0), Write(lbl0))

        # Iteration 1
        z1_val = z0_val**2 + c_val
        z1_point = plane.n2p(z1_val)
        dot1 = Dot(z1_point, color=RED, radius=0.08)
        arrow1 = Arrow(dot0.get_center(), dot1.get_center(), buff=0.1, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)

        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow1), FadeIn(dot1))

        # 4. Symbolic Logic on the Grid
        chaos_text = Text("Chaotic Motion", font_size=22, color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(chaos_text, "F3")
        
        rect = SurroundingRectangle(chaos_text, color=RED, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(
            Write(chaos_text),
            Create(rect)
        )

        # Final Wait
        self.wait(3)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard and outline
        title_text = "The Boundary of Chaos: Julia Sets"
        lecture_lines = [
            "The Julia set is the boundary of these behaviors.",
            "It separates points that stay from points that escape.",
            "On this edge, movement is unpredictable and chaotic.",
            "Zooming in reveals infinite, self-similar fractal patterns.",
            "This boundary contains the essence of holomorphic dynamics."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Hex colors as per storyboard - Cast to ManimColor to support interpolate_color
        COLOR_C = ManimColor("#FFFF00")
        COLOR_DARK_BLUE = ManimColor("#00008B")
        COLOR_CYAN = ManimColor("#00FFFF")
        COLOR_BOUNDARY = ManimColor("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_C)
        c_val = MathTex("c = -0.4 + 0.6i", color=COLOR_C)
        # Position at B3
        self.place_at_grid(c_val, "B3", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(c_val))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_CYAN)
        
        # Grid parameters for the fractal area (C2 to F5)
        res = 20
        tl_pos = self.grid["C2"]
        br_pos = self.grid["F5"]
        
        total_width = br_pos[0] - tl_pos[0]
        total_height = tl_pos[1] - br_pos[1]
        sq_size = min(total_width, total_height) / res
        
        grid_squares = VGroup()
        c_complex = complex(-0.4, 0.6)
        
        for row in range(res):
            for col in range(res):
                x = tl_pos[0] + col * sq_size + sq_size/2
                y = tl_pos[1] - row * sq_size - sq_size/2
                
                sq = Square(side_length=sq_size, stroke_width=0.3, stroke_color=WHITE)
                sq.move_to([x, y, 0])
                
                re = -1.5 + (col / res) * 3.0
                im = 1.5 - (row / res) * 3.0
                z = complex(re, im)
                
                escape_iter = 0
                max_iter = 20
                for _ in range(max_iter):
                    if abs(z) > 2:
                        break
                    z = z**2 + c_complex
                    escape_iter += 1
                
                sq.escape_iter = escape_iter
                sq.max_iter = max_iter
                grid_squares.add(sq)

        self.play(FadeIn(grid_squares, lag_ratio=0.001), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_CYAN)
        
        fill_anims = []
        for sq in grid_squares:
            if sq.escape_iter == sq.max_iter:
                target_color = BLACK
            else:
                # Use ManimColor interpolation
                target_color = interpolate_color(COLOR_DARK_BLUE, COLOR_CYAN, sq.escape_iter / sq.max_iter)
            
            fill_anims.append(sq.animate.set_fill(target_color, opacity=1).set_stroke(width=0))
            
        self.play(AnimationGroup(*fill_anims, lag_ratio=0.002), run_time=2.0)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_BOUNDARY)
        
        boundary_sqs = VGroup(*[sq for sq in grid_squares if 4 < sq.escape_iter < sq.max_iter])
        
        self.play(
            AnimationGroup(*[Indicate(sq, color=COLOR_BOUNDARY) for sq in boundary_sqs], lag_ratio=0.01),
            run_time=2
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_BOUNDARY)
        
        # Pick a target point on the boundary for zooming
        zoom_target = grid_squares[8 * res + 14].get_center()
        
        self.play(
            grid_squares.animate.scale(5, about_point=zoom_target),
            c_val.animate.scale(0.7).move_to(self.grid["B1"]),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(3)

        # Retrieve content from shared state

        lecture_lines = [
            "We iterate the function z squared plus c.",
            "The Mandelbrot set maps every possible value of c.",
            "Points inside represent parameters with connected Julia sets.",
            "Each tiny bulb corresponds to a unique fractal world.",
            "It is the ultimate dictionary of complex iteration."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Define custom colors as per visual guidelines
        COLOR_FORMULA = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_MANDELBROT = "#FF00FF"
        COLOR_PLANE = BLUE_D
        COLOR_SWEEP = WHITE
        COLOR_THUMB = ORANGE
        COLOR_MINI = PINK

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Set z_0 = 0 in #FFFFFF and show the formula z_{n+1} = z_n^2 + c.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_FORMULA)
        
        formula = MathTex("z_{n+1} = z_n^2 + c", color=COLOR_FORMULA)
        z0_label = MathTex("z_0 = 0", color=COLOR_FORMULA)
        formula_group = VGroup(formula, z0_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        
        # Position in top-right area (Row B)
        self.place_in_area(formula_group, "B2", "B4", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(formula), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(z0_label, shift=UP*0.2), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Sweep the complex plane, coloring points that don't escape in black (#000000).
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Initialize a coordinate system (NumberPlane)
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2.5, 1.0, 1],
            y_range=[-1.2, 1.2, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": COLOR_PLANE, "stroke_opacity": 0.3},
            axis_config={"stroke_opacity": 0.5}
        )
        # Position plane in the central/lower right area (C2 to E5)
        self.place_in_area(plane, "C2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Visual sweep line effect
        sweep_line = Line(
            plane.get_left(), plane.get_right(), 
            color=COLOR_SWEEP, stroke_width=2, stroke_opacity=0.6
        )
        sweep_line.set_y(plane.get_top()[1])
        
        self.play(Create(plane), run_time=1.5)
        # Linear sweep across the plane's vertical range
        self.play(
            sweep_line.animate.move_to(plane.get_bottom()),
            run_time=2.5,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.play(FadeOut(sweep_line))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Reveal the iconic Mandelbrot bulb and cardioid shape with a #FF00FF outline.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_MANDELBROT)
        
        # Geometric approximation of the Mandelbrot cardioid
        # c(t) = 1/4 * (2*exp(it) - exp(i2t))
        m_cardioid = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: plane.coords_to_point(
                0.25 * (2 * np.cos(t) - np.cos(2 * t)),
                0.25 * (2 * np.sin(t) - np.sin(2 * t))
            ),
            t_range=[0, TAU],
            color=COLOR_MANDELBROT,
            stroke_width=3
        )
        
        # Geometric approximation of the period-2 bulb (Circle at -1, radius 1/4)
        bulb_center = plane.coords_to_point(-1, 0)
        # Calculate radius in screen units based on plane scale
        bulb_radius = 0.25 * (plane.get_x_unit_size())
        m_bulb = Circle(radius=bulb_radius, color=COLOR_MANDELBROT, stroke_width=3)
        m_bulb.move_to(bulb_center)
        
        m_set_outline = VGroup(m_cardioid, m_bulb)
        
        # Solid fill to denote points inside the set
        m_set_filled = m_set_outline.copy().set_fill(BLACK, opacity=1).set_stroke(width=1)
        
        self.play(Create(m_set_outline), run_time=2)
        self.play(FadeIn(m_set_filled))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Small thumbnails of different Julia sets appear around the main set.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_THUMB)
        
        # Representative points on the boundary for Julia set samples
        julia_locs = [
            plane.coords_to_point(-0.1, 0.7),
            plane.coords_to_point(-0.8, 0.15),
            plane.coords_to_point(0.28, 0.45),
            plane.coords_to_point(-1.25, 0)
        ]
        
        thumbnails = VGroup()
        for i, pt in enumerate(julia_locs):
            # Complex-looking polygon shapes representing localized fractal structures
            sides = 10 + i * 2
            thumb = RegularPolygon(n=sides, color=COLOR_THUMB, fill_opacity=0.5).scale(0.12)
            thumb.move_to(pt)
            thumbnails.add(thumb)
            
        self.play(
            LaggedStart(
                *[FadeIn(t, scale=1.3) for t in thumbnails],
                lag_ratio=0.4
            ),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Scale the entire view to show the 'mini-mandelbrots' along the filaments.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_MINI)
        
        # Create a "mini-mandelbrot" copy at a filament point (e.g., the tail)
        mini_m_loc = plane.coords_to_point(-1.75, 0)
        mini_m = m_set_outline.copy().scale(0.12).set_color(COLOR_MINI)
        mini_m.move_to(mini_m_loc)
        
        # Combine all visual elements for a synchronized zoom
        all_elements = VGroup(plane, m_set_outline, m_set_filled, thumbnails, mini_m)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(mini_m))
        # Zoom centered on the mini-mandelbrot location

        )

        self.play(Indicate(mini_m, color=COLOR_MINI, scale_factor=1.2))
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data
        title_text = "Conclusion: Beauty in Complexity"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Simple mathematical rules generate infinite, non-repeating beauty.",
            "These dynamics model everything from weather to fluid flow.",
            "One simple equation contains an entire universe of art."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_BEAUTY = YELLOW
        COLOR_MODEL = "#00FFFF" # Cyan
        COLOR_ART = WHITE
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Transition from the Mandelbrot set to a montage of natural fractals (leaves, clouds).
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_BEAUTY))
        
        # Mandelbrot Set Equation (Representative)
        mandel_eq = MathTex("z_{n+1} = z_n^2 + c", color=COLOR_BEAUTY)

        self.play(Write(mandel_eq))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Natural Fractal Elements (Montage)

        cloud_icon = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=0.2, color=LIGHT_GREY, fill_opacity=0.7),
            Circle(radius=0.25, color=LIGHT_GREY, fill_opacity=0.7).shift(RIGHT*0.2),
            Circle(radius=0.2, color=LIGHT_GREY, fill_opacity=0.7).shift(LEFT*0.2)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(cloud_icon, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)
        cloud_label = Text("Clouds", font_size=18, color=LIGHT_GREY)
        self.place_at_grid(cloud_label, 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # 3. Crystal (using a polygon)
        crystal_icon = RegularPolygon(n=6, color=BLUE_A, fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(crystal_icon, 'E3', scale_factor=0.7)
        crystal_label = Text("Crystals", font_size=18, color=BLUE_A)
        self.place_at_grid(crystal_label, 'E4', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Transition to Montage
        montage_group = VGroup(leaf_icon, leaf_label, cloud_icon, cloud_label, crystal_icon, crystal_label)
        
        self.play(
            mandel_eq.animate.scale(0.6).move_to(self.grid['B5']),
            FadeIn(montage_group, shift=UP),
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Pulse the entire screen with vibrant, shifting rainbow colors (#FF0000 to #0000FF).
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_MODEL))
        
        # Create full-screen rectangle for pulse
        pulse_overlay = Rectangle(
            width=config.frame_width,
            height=config.frame_height,
            stroke_width=0,
            fill_opacity=0.0
        ).set_z_index(-1) # Behind everything
        self.add(pulse_overlay)
        
        # Shifting rainbow pulse
        rainbow_colors = ["#FF0000", "#FF7F00", "#FFFF00", "#00FF00", "#0000FF"]
        for col in rainbow_colors:
            self.play(
                pulse_overlay.animate.set_fill(color=col, opacity=0.25),
                run_time=0.4,
                rate_func=smooth
            )
        
        self.play(pulse_overlay.animate.set_fill(opacity=0.0), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade everything out to a final 'Thank You' in #FFFFFF.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_ART))
        
        thank_you_text = Text("Thank You", font_size=48, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(thank_you_text, 'B3', 'E5')
        
        # Group current elements (excluding title and lecture)
        current_visuals = VGroup(mandel_eq, montage_group, pulse_overlay)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(current_visuals),
            Write(thank_you_text)
        )
        
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: Journey into Chaos: Holomorphic Dynamics and Iterated Functions
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate STEM students or advanced high school students with a background in basic algebra and complex numbers.

sections.title: The Feedback Loop: What is Iteration?
sections.content: Introduce the core concept of iteration: taking the output of a function and plugging it back in as the next input. Visually, this is represented as a 'feedback machine' where a value cycles through a process repeatedly.
sections.example: Imagine a 'Digital Chameleon' named Echo. Echo's color value is a number. If the rule is f(x) = x², and Echo starts at 2, his color values evolve: 2 -> 4 -> 16 -> 256. He quickly explodes into brightness!

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Complex Plane as a Playground
sections.content: Briefly review complex numbers (z = x + iy) not as just numbers, but as 2D coordinates. Explain that squaring a complex number involves 'stretching' its distance from the center and 'rotating' its angle. This geometric transformation is the engine of holomorphic dynamics.
sections.example: Visualizing a grid on a rubber sheet: squaring the complex number 'i' (at 90 degrees) rotates it to -1 (180 degrees). Multiplying acts like a dance across the 2D plane.

sections.title: Orbits: The Path of a Point
sections.content: Define an 'Orbit' as the sequence of points generated by iteration. Points can have three fates: escaping to infinity, converging to a fixed point (attractor), or wandering forever in a cycle/chaos.
sections.example: Think of a marble on a terrain. If we iterate f(z) = z², a marble starting at z=0.5 spirals inward to the center (0), while a marble at z=2.0 shoots off the edge of the map.

sections.title: The Boundary of Chaos: Julia Sets
sections.content: Introduce the Julia Set as the 'borderline' between points that escape and points that stay. On one side, the behavior is stable (Fatou Set); on the boundary, the behavior is chaotic and infinitely complex.
sections.example: The 'Douady's Rabbit' Julia set. Visual: An intricate, fractal rabbit-shaped boundary where points right on the edge of the 'fur' don't know whether to stay inside or fly away, creating beautiful, self-similar patterns.

sections.title: The Map of All Maps: The Mandelbrot Set
sections.content: Explain the Mandelbrot Set as a 'parameter map' for the function f(z) = z² + c. Instead of tracking one starting point, we test different values of 'c' to see which ones produce a connected Julia set. It is a dictionary of all possible behaviors.
sections.example: Zooming into the Mandelbrot 'Apple-Man' shape. Every tiny 'bulb' on the set represents a different 'c' value that creates a unique fractal world (Julia set) for our 'Digital Chameleon' to live in.

sections.title: Conclusion: Beauty in Complexity
sections.content: Summarize how simple rules (iteration of holomorphic functions) lead to infinite, non-repeating complexity. Emphasize that these dynamics are the foundation for understanding weather patterns, fluid flow, and fractal geometry.
sections.example: A final zoom-out from a fractal 'seahorse tail' back to the original simple equation z = z² + c, showing how one line of math contains an entire universe of art.
